title: Introduce staged intake intent and profile shadowing for safe, measurable model rollouts
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Context: As model intake velocity grows we need a lightweight safe path to stage new model manifests and performance profiles without impacting live serving. This PR adds a 'staged intake intent' concept plus 'profile shadowing' so teams can register candidate model versions, run sampled traffic/probes against shadowed profiles, and automatically synthesize a preview changelog describing measured regressions and cost delta. Motivation: reduce risk of blind rollouts, make onboarding telemetry-driven, and provide concise release-ready notes for model ops. Summary of features: 1) staged intake manifest schema (staged_intake.yaml) with intent metadata (owner, canary-criteria, probe-sets, retention-ttl); 2) profile-shadow runner service that can accept a staged manifest and shadow live traffic into a sandboxed profile evaluation pipeline (local kv-cache isolation + cost telemetry); 3) probe sampler that runs a configurable subset of promptsets (promptset refs in manifest) and computes key deltas (latency P95, tokens-per-request, quality-regression score) and stores a compact report; 4) changelog synthesizer that takes probe reports and generates a draft release blurb (short, medium, long) with links to artifacts; 5) lightweight web preview in registry UI (api route /staged-preview/:id) that renders the manifest + probe deltas + proposed release snippet. Implementation notes: aim for minimal runtime impact by making shadowing opt-in per manifest and sampling at route-level; identity-preserving telemetry tags are stripped before storage to meet compliance; manifests are immutable once marked "candidate", and shadow runs are tagged with provenance (uploader, commit, manifest-hash). Backwards compatibility: existing manifest ingestion remains unchanged unless a staged intent field is present. Checklist: - [x] manifest schema and validation - [x] profile-shadow runner and sandbox isolation - [x] probe sampler + three default promptsets - [x] changelog synthesizer with templating - [x] unit + integration tests for ingestion and draft generation - [x] docs/registry/staged-intake.md draft - [x] lightweight UI preview endpoint - [x] privacy/stripper for telemetry. Risks and mitigations: memory overhead during shadow runs mitigated by limiting concurrent shadow workers and reusing KV cache objects; behavioral regressions are surfaced only in preview and do not affect routing. Next steps: allow autoscheduling of shadow runs based on traffic thresholds, add RBAC controls for who can mark a manifest candidate, and wire preview generation to the release-notes exporter.

release_notes: Added staged intake manifests and profile shadowing to enable safe, observable model rollouts. Includes a probe sampler and changelog synthesizer that produces draft release notes with measured perf/quality deltas. Opt-in feature behind staged intent in manifests.
notes_for_operators: To enable preview runs in Dedicated clusters set registry.config.shadow_workers>0 and configure probe promptsets. Shadow runs are resource-limited; monitor metrics shadow_worker_memory and shadow_run_count. Use registry CLI 'registry preview publish <manifest>' to trigger manual runs.
qa_summary: QA ran a 48-hour shadow campaign against the prod-like perf-canary using three promptsets. Results were stable: latency delta <= 2ms P95 for 2/3 promptsets, quality score regression detected on one conversational promptset and surfaced in draft changelog. No leaks of identity tokens observed.
